UKRI-sector-transition-ukri-policy-fello.heading: How we will assess your application

blocks.text: When you apply for this opportunity, we will ask you for information about your project. The information we’ll use to assess your application will be your responses to questions about:
Vision
Approach to co-design
Applicant capability to deliver
Impact, knowledge exchange, outcomes and outputs
Career development
Employing organisation support
Resources and costs
Career stage
Declaration of interest
Trusted research & innovation (TR&I)
Find details of assessment questions and criteria under the ‘Questions we will ask you’ heading in the ‘How to apply’ section.
We reserve the right to modify the assessment process as needed.
Timing
We aim to complete the assessment process and make funding decisions within 24 weeks of the closing date.
Initial application check
When you submit your application, we will check that:
all applicants and team members are eligible for the funding opportunity
the application meets the funding opportunity aims and criteria
Assessment panel
If your application passes the initial check, it will go to assessment panel of academic and non-academic experts to assess the quality of your application.

If your application does not pass the initial check, it will not go any further. We will email you to let you know your application did not pass the initial check within four weeks of submitting your application.
We will assess your application using the following process. In the case of unusually high demand, an initial sift prior to shortlisting may be carried out.
Each panel member will independently:

assess your application against the assessment criteria for this funding opportunity, as set out in the UKRI Funding Finder guidance and the additional essential criteria in the fellowship position specifications
make an evidence-based judgment and score your application out of 10 to inform shortlisting
Shortlisting outcomes will be dependent on both:
receiving a competitive score
the number of interview slots each fellowship host partner is able to offer
You will be informed of shortlisting outcomes by 21 May 2027. All applicants will receive feedback from the panel assessment process.
Expert review and moderation panel
If your application passes the initial check, it will go to expert review.
If your application does not pass the initial check, it will not go any further.
We will email you to let you know if your application passes the initial check or not. We aim to email you within four weeks of submitting your application.
We will invite at least three experts to independently:
review your application against the assessment criteria for this funding opportunity
make comments on your application
If your application gets enough support:
it will go to panel
you’ll be able to respond to expert reviewer comments
If your application does not get enough support, we will reject it.
Responding to expert reviewer comments
You will have 14 days to respond to comments.
We will email you to let you know when they are available and how to reply.
Scoring
We will then send your application to a panel of reviewers qualified to assess it. They will score your application based on:
the information provided in your application
the expert reviews of your application
your responses to reviewer comments
Interviews

If your application is competitive enough then it will be shortlisted for an interview by representatives of the relevant host partner. This interview panel will then evaluate the merits of your application, assessing both the essential and the desirable criteria in the fellowship position specifications, before making funding recommendations to UKRI.

Interviews are expected to take place in the week commencing 21 June 2027 and will be managed by the host partner departments, mayoral strategic authorities, regional partnerships or What Works Networks.
Final funding decision
UKRI will make the final funding decisions.
We expect the funding decision will be communicated in July 2027.
Host partners conducting interviews will provide feedback to all applicants who are interviewed.
Getting feedback on your application
Host partners conducting interviews will provide feedback to all applicants who are interviewed.
All applicants for this opportunity will receive feedback.
For further details on how we assess opportunity applications, read How we make decisions .
Publication of outcomes
We publish information about successful applications and their awards on Gateway to Research.
Principles of assessment
We support the San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment .
This recognises the need to improve the ways in which researchers and the outputs of scholarly research are evaluated.
We also recognise the relationship between research assessment and research integrity.
Use of AI in assessment
Expert reviewers and panellists are not allowed to use AI tools in their assessment in any way. This is to help keep the ideas in your application confidential.
Information sharing with co-funders

UKRI will need to share the application and any personal information that it contains with the host partners so that they can participate in the assessment process. For more information on how the host uses personal information please see the specific fellowship position.

Personal data provided in applications may be shared with any grant co-funders for the purpose of awarding, administration and evaluation of grants. This includes the Department for Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) who provide co-funding to the Natural Hazards and Resilience Fellowships, part of the UKRI Policy Fellowships programme.

consortium.quote: Unless otherwise provided for in the specific call/topic conditions, only legal entities forming a consortium are eligible to participate in actions provided that the consortium includes, as beneficiaries, three legal entities independent from each other and each established in a different country as follows: – at least one independent legal entity established in a Member State; and – at least two other independent legal entities, each established in different Member States or Associated Countries.
